task: Quantitative bicondylar-jaw lever model of the TMJ: (1) a sagittal single-fulcrum static-equilibrium model deriving the molar/incisor maximal-bite-force ratio purely from bite-point-to-condyle moment-arm geometry (proven algebraically independent of muscle-force magnitude, PCSA, or specific tension), forcing the condylar reaction force (which a naive fixed-fulcrum model implicitly sets to zero) to be computed explicitly and shown large and non-zero; (2) a coronal two-condyle model of unilateral molar biting deriving the balancing-side>working-side condylar reaction asymmetry from a genuine 2-support statics solve, sweeping the working-side muscle-activation fraction as a forced adversary; (3) a kinematic rotate-then-translate model of interincisal opening ROM; (4) two perturbation adversaries (muscle weakness, disc-displacement delayed translation) plus the coronal model itself as the third (unilateral asymmetric loading).
confidence_tier: geometrically-forced and multi-anchor-triangulated for the ORDINAL/ratio claims (molar>incisor bite force ratio and the balancing>working condylar-reaction asymmetry are proven numerically to be independent of the muscle-force-magnitude parameters, not fitted to hit the measured values) -- DOMAIN_CONSENSUS/estimated tier for absolute force and ROM magnitudes, since several geometric nuisance parameters (elevator moment arm, intercondylar width, transverse bite/muscle-attachment fractions, rotation angle) are anatomical-range estimates rather than literature-pinned this session, disclosed in full.
raw_results: data/msk_smoketest/tmj_lever_model/tmj_lever_model_results.json (+ sagittal_sweep_raw.csv n=4000, coronal_sweep_raw.csv n=1500, kinematic_sweep_raw.csv n=36)

F1_molar_incisor_ratio_geometric.claim: molar/incisor max-bite-force ratio emerges from bite-point-to-condyle moment-arm geometry alone (d_incisor/d_molar), independent of muscle-force magnitude

F2_condylar_reaction_nonzero_and_ordered.claim: condylar reaction force R_condyle = F_muscle - F_bite is large and non-zero (falsifying a fixed-fulcrum-ignoring-joint-reaction adversary), and joint-load-per-unit-bite-force is higher at incisor than molar (molar is more joint-efficient)

F3_balancing_working_asymmetry.claim: unilateral molar bite produces balancing-side condylar reaction > working-side condylar reaction, robust to a forced working-side-EMG-bias adversary
F3_balancing_working_asymmetry.note_hand_algebra_error_caught: an initial hand-derived estimate suggested a finite crossover near alpha=0.94; the machine-computed dense sweep found none in [0.5,0.999] -- the hand estimate had the alpha-dependence direction backwards
F3_balancing_working_asymmetry.note_compression_only_constraint: unconstrained solve gives working-side reaction R_R<0 (tensile) in 100% of sweep at alpha=0.5; a real compression-only TMJ would clamp this to 0 and push the remainder onto the balancing side, making the true asymmetry >= the reported one, corroborated by Osborn & Baragar 1992's own compression-only joint-force-direction constraint

F4_kinematic_rom.claim: rotation-chord + measured-translation reproduces the real ~46-52mm interincisal opening band
F4_kinematic_rom.limitation: Chen 1998 (PMID 9590523) shows real opening is simultaneous rotation+translation, not additively separable -- the idealized additive model runs high, disclosed not hidden
F4_kinematic_rom.verdict: PASS (weak pre-registered overlap criterion; stronger median-match criterion would not be met, disclosed)

F5_perturbation_adversaries.unilateral_asymmetric_loading: = F3_balancing_working_asymmetry above (the coronal model IS this adversary)

decorrelated_anchor: gnathodynamometry-measured molar/incisor max-bite-force ratio (Waltimo & Kononen, 2 independent device-generations/cohorts, PMID 7484109 + 8322012) tested against a geometry-ONLY predicted ratio that is numerically proven independent of muscle-force magnitude (identity diff 4.4e-16) -- a clean decorrelation between the force-calibration side of the model and the falsifier; triangulated by Hylander 1975's independent EMG-based balancing>working conclusion (PMID 1101706) and Shi et al 2012's cross-species multibody-dynamics-optimization confirmation of the same asymmetry in macaque (PMID 22721994) -- two different eras, methods, and species converging on the same qualitative result.
honest_gaps: r_muscle (elevator moment arm about condyle), intercondylar width, transverse bite/muscle-attachment fractions, and rotation angle are anatomical-range estimates swept over a disclosed plausible band, not literature-pinned this session

central absolute bite-force estimate runs ~44-60% high vs measured (passes only the generous 0.3-3.0x regime band, not a tight match), driven mainly by reusing this repo's limb-muscle-sourced 15-100 N/cm2 specific-tension convention as a disclosed cross-domain proxy
temporalis total PCSA (14.25cm2) is mean-of-range x 6 portions, not a literature-reported sum
masseter PCSA uses an MRI anatomical CSA (Daboul 2018), not a fiber-corrected PCSA -- likely a conservative underestimate for this pennate muscle

kinematic model's additive rotation+translation decomposition runs high (median 58.5mm vs ~46-52mm measured) because real motion is simultaneous not sequential (Chen 1998) -- disclosed, not hidden, only 19.4% of the swept grid lands inside the tight measured band even though the full range overlaps it
the working-side-tensile finding's exact magnitude is sensitive to un-pinned transverse geometry; only the ordinal balancing>working claim is robust
Pruim 1980 and Weijs & Hillen 1985 are existence-verified only (abstract text unavailable, pre-abstract-era MEDLINE records) -- never quoted or used as a numeric source

single maximal-static-clench scenario throughout; no dynamic chewing-cycle timing or EMG-driven optimization over the indeterminate muscle set (Nickel et al 2003 shows the real system optimizes; this model uses one determinate resultant)

Marpaung/Kalaykova/Naeije 2014's 44.8% MRI disc-displacement prevalence is a referred/clinical sample (n=53), not general population -- must not be conflated with Naeije 2013's general-population 18-35% review figure
no disc/cartilage contact-PRESSURE mechanics modeled -- this is the lever/reaction-force layer only; contact pressure at the disc-condyle-fossa interface is an open next step
proposed_cell: TMJ_lever_cert follow-up: (1) replace the swept anatomical-range geometric nuisance parameters with coordinates digitized from a real CT/CBCT mandible or open craniofacial multibody model; (2) replace the coronal model's unconstrained linear solve with a proper compression-only (non-negative-reaction / linear-complementarity) contact formulation to resolve the working-side-tensile finding exactly; (3) replace the additive rotation+translation kinematic idealization with a genuinely simultaneous single-time-parameter rigid-body chain informed by Chen 1998's instantaneous-center-of-rotation data; (4) extend to disc/cartilage contact-pressure mechanics at the condyle-disc-fossa interface, following MECHANISM_CARTILAGE_CONTACT.md's existing tibiofemoral/patellofemoral pattern, to let a future cert test disc displacement as a pressure (not just translation-timing) failure mode.
couples_to: cervical/postural chain (mandible muscular sling + hyoid-suspended muscles -- open coupling, not modeled)
